item.title: Living in Lentate and working in Ticino: border crossing
item.description: Lentate sul Seveso, province of Milan, is a strategic residential choice for border workers. Discover tax advantages, G Permit, transfer procedures and checklists.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Lentate sul Seveso is a Lombard municipality in the province of Milan, bordering Ticino - G border workers pay withholding tax in Switzerland; tax credit in Italy avoids double taxation - New Border Workers Agreement 2024: exemption €7.500 (old border workers) or €10.000 (new) - LAMal (Swiss health insurance) is a right of option; deductible CHF 300–2.500
## Key facts - **What**: Lentate sul Seveso is a Lombard border municipality with Ticino - Where: Province of Milan, Lombardy (Italy) - Who: Border workers with Permit G who reside in Italy and work in Switzerland - When: New Border Workers Agreement effective from January 1, 2024 - Permit: Permit G mandatory; AVS deductions 5.3% (employee), AD/AC 1.1%, LAINF 0.7–1.5% - Taxation: Withholding tax in Switzerland; tax credit in Italy (quadro CE of the 730)
Lentate sul Seveso is a municipality in northern Lombardy, in the province of Milan, strategically located north of the capital. Its proximity to the Swiss border, particularly to the Ticino border crossings (Brogeda, Gaggiolo, Ponte Tresa), makes it an interesting residential choice for those who decide to work in Ticino while maintaining their residence in Italy.
Those who live in Lentate and work in Switzerland (Canton Ticino) fall under the legal regime of border workers with Permit G. This status entails specific rights and duties from a fiscal, pension, and insurance perspective, regulated by the New Border Workers Agreement signed on December 23, 2020, and effective from January 1, 2024.
### Lentate and the border worker's geography
Lentate sul Seveso extends into the Lombard plain, north of Milan, in a position that facilitates access to the main border crossings with Ticino. The proximity to the Brogeda, Gaggiolo, and Ponte Tresa crossings is a crucial logistical factor: border workers can reach Ticino work centers (Lugano, Mendrisio, Bellinzona, Locarno) through daily commuting. The town is located in the heart of the Lombard industrial area, with direct access to the A4 (Milan-Chiasso) and A9 highways towards Como and Lake Como. This geographical scenario is particularly relevant for a border worker who wants to maintain legal residence in Italy while benefiting from access to the Ticino job market.
### The border worker condition: fiscal and contributory regime
The border worker with Permit G who works in Ticino is subject to withholding tax directly from the Swiss salary. The rate depends on the canton and income bracket, but AVS (old-age and disability insurance) contributions for the employee amount to 5.3%, to which complementary insurance contributions are added (AD/AC 1.1%, LAINF 0.7–1.5%, LPP depending on age).
In Italy, the border worker declares the foreign income in the quadro CE of the 730/PF and accesses the tax credit to avoid double taxation, provided for by the Convention between Italy and Switzerland (December 9, 1976). This mechanism allows for not paying taxes twice on the same income.
The New Border Workers Agreement has introduced, from January 1, 2024, exemption thresholds with respect to worldwide net income: border workers already in this status before July 17, 2023, benefit from an annual exemption of €7.500 (transitional regime 2024–2033), while new border workers have the right to a franchise of €10.000. These thresholds represent an important element in personal tax planning. Law 83 of June 13, 2023, ratified the new agreement in Italy. ### Practical and economic advantages of transferring to Lentate for the border crossing
The choice to reside in Lentate while working in Ticino has tangible advantages, especially in economic and housing terms. The cost of living in Lombardy remains on average lower than that of the Canton of Ticino: rents, services and food are generally less expensive in the territory of Lentate than in Ticino centres of the same size (Lugano, Mendrisio).
In addition, the border worker resident in Italy benefits from the Swiss social security system (AVS/AI) through the contributions withheld on the Swiss paycheck, accumulating years of contribution that translate into a pension upon reaching retirement age. The LPP (Occupational Pension Fund, second pillar) is mandatory for those who exceed a salary threshold: the Swiss employer pays contributions that the employee can redeem or transfer to facilities in Italy in the event of termination of the employment relationship.
The possibility of option on LAMal (Swiss health insurance) represents an additional advantage: the border worker with G Permit has the right to choose to insure with a Swiss insurer, potentially advantageous if the income is high, or to keep the insurance in Italy. Adult deductibles in Switzerland start at CHF 300 and can go up to CHF 2,500, depending on your chosen coverage.
### Disadvantages and considerations
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### Procedure and checklist for moving to Lentate as a cross-border worker
Deciding to live in Lentate and work in Ticino requires a series of administrative and contractual steps. The logical sequence begins with signing the employment contract with a Ticino company (or accepting the offer if the move involves a job change).
**Step 1: Permit G**
Obtain the Permit G from the competent Swiss authorities (Migration Office – SEM/Cantonal Migration Section). This authorizes the cross-border worker to reside in Italy and work in Switzerland. The Ticino employer, except in very rare normative exceptions, must submit the work authorization request on behalf of the employee. Processing times are generally 4–8 weeks. The Permit G is valid for one year (automatic renewal if employment continues).
Step 2: INPS Registration and Tax Residence
Once hired, the cross-border worker must register with INPS as a direct foreign worker. At the same time, they must notify the Italian Revenue Agency of their Italian tax residence (Lentate sul Seveso) and foreign (Swiss) income for inclusion in the 730 or 770 form (income tax return). The deadline for the annual declaration in Italy is generally June 30 of the year following the year in which the income was received.
Step 3: Health Insurance (LAMal)
Within the first month of employment in Switzerland, the cross-border worker must choose whether to remain insured with an Italian insurer (continuity with the Italian national health system) or opt for Swiss LAMal. Choosing LAMal involves enrolling with one of the health insurance funds recognized by the Ticino canton; this option is irreversible for the first year.
Step 4: AVS/LPP Contributions
Contributions for Swiss social security (AVS/AI/IPG) and professional pension (LPP) are automatically deducted from the paycheck. The cross-border worker does not need to take additional actions, except to verify the correct application of the rates (e.g., 5.3% AVS for the employee). It is advisable to request an annual AVS statement to verify the accrual of contributions.
### Documents to Prepare
A cross-border worker moving to Lentate should gather: valid passport and/or identity card; residence certificate from the local authority of Lentate; employment contract with the signature of the Ticino employer; Italian tax code; criminal record extract (casellario giudiziario); for LAMal: insurance number (if already in Switzerland) or request for new enrollment; copy of the Permit G request (when submitted).
### Deadlines and Annual Calendar
The main deadlines for a cross-border worker residing in Lentate are: January 31 (INPS contribution declaration deadline); June 30 (730/PF income tax return deadline in Italy); annually (Permit G renewal, usually automatic); annually, March-April (payment of the second IMU installment, if a property owner in Italy).
### When It Really Pays to Move: Decision Elements
The choice to live in Lentate rather than in Ticino is advantageous when the housing cost differential (rent, mortgage) between Lentate and Ticino is significant (at least 25–30% monthly savings); commuting is sustainable (easy access to border crossings); the family situation is stable (spouse with a job in Italy, children enrolled in Italian schools); the income is such that it does not fully utilize Italian tax deductions (thus the Swiss tax credit covers most of the taxation).
Conversely, moving to Lentate becomes disadvantageous if commuting is particularly burdensome, if the spouse works in Ticino (increases transportation costs), or if there is an intention to purchase a house in Lentate with a mortgage: in this case, the tax advantage could be eroded by the costs of interest and property management in Italy.
To verify in detail whether moving to Lentate is advantageous in your specific case, use the [salary calculator](nav:calculator) of Frontaliere Ticino: this tool simulates the monthly and annual net income considering Swiss taxation, Italian tax credit, AVS/LPP contributions, and LAMal choice. You can thus compare different income scenarios and tax deadlines.
For more information on transportation costs and [public transport in Ticino](nav:transport), as well as [information on border crossings](nav:border), consult the dedicated resources.

item.title: Living in Lazzate, working in Ticino: the guide
item.description: Lazzate offers lower housing prices for border workers. Discover travel times, commuting costs, taxation (tax at source), G Permit and step-by-step procedure.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Lazzate: Lombardy municipality close to Chiasso, Brogeda, Gaggiolo border crossings - Permit G required; withholding tax deducted in Switzerland - New Cross-Border Workers Agreement (effective January 1, 2024): different regimes for old and new cross-border workers - LAMal mandatory; cross-border workers have the right to choose
## Key facts - **What**: Residential move to Lazzate + employment in Ticino - Where: Lazzate (Varese, Lombardy) — access via Chiasso, Brogeda, Gaggiolo - Who: Cross-border workers category Permit G (employees) - When: Permit G renewable annually in January - Tax treatment: Withholding tax in Switzerland; double taxation avoided with tax credit in Italy (form CE 730) - Convention: Italy-Switzerland of December 9, 1976 - New Agreement: Effective from January 1, 2024 (ratification IT Law 83 of June 13, 2023); old cross-border workers exemption €7,500, new allowance €10,000
Lazzate, a municipality in the province of Varese, Lombardy, is increasingly attracting cross-border workers drawn by the lower cost of living while maintaining the advantages of a Ticino job. Its proximity to border crossings (Chiasso, Brogeda, Gaggiolo) and reasonable travel times to major Ticino centers (Lugano, Mendrisio, Bellinzona, Locarno) make it a strategic choice. However, to move and work in Switzerland as a cross-border worker, specific permits (Permit G), proper tax declaration, and a clear understanding of the Italo-Swiss tax regimes are necessary.
The New Cross-Border Workers Agreement, effective January 1, 2024, has significantly changed the taxation and refund methods for those living in Italy and working in Switzerland. This guide accompanies the cross-border worker candidate through the requirements, economic implications, and essential administrative procedures.
### Lazzate and the Ticino border
Lazzate is located in the province of Varese, Lombardy, a short distance from the main access points to Ticino. This geographical proximity makes it attractive for those who want to reduce housing costs without moving too far from their workplace. Travel times to major Ticino centers remain reasonable: from Lazzate to Lugano about 1 hour, to Mendrisio about 30–40 minutes, to Bellinzona about 1 hour and 30 minutes, to Locarno about 2 hours.
Daily commuting, however, involves significant additional costs that each cross-border worker candidate should carefully evaluate: fuel (about CHF 150–300 per month), Swiss vignette (CHF 40 per year), A2 and A9 motorway tolls (CHF 80–120 per month), car wear (increase 25–30%), parking in Ticino urban centers (CHF 100–200 per month), and car insurance (higher premiums in Italy compared to Switzerland).
### Permit G: the requirements
To work in Switzerland as a cross-border worker, the first step is to obtain Permit G from the SEM (State Secretariat for Migration). This permit is reserved for cross-border dependent workers who reside permanently in Italy and cross the border daily or regularly. Permit G is valid for one year and is renewable without interruption, provided the employment relationship continues.
The procedure requires a letter of employment from the Ticino employer, a signed employment contract, the Italian identity document, and a municipal residence certificate in Lazzate. Processing times vary from 2 to 4 weeks; renewal occurs in January of each year.
Once Permit G is obtained, the cross-border worker is automatically enrolled in the Swiss social security system: old-age and survivors' insurance (AVS), disability insurance (AI), loss of earnings compensation (IPG), accident insurance (LAINF), and pension fund (LPP according to age group). These contributions are deducted directly from the Swiss paycheck according to federal (AVS/AI/IPG 5.3% for the employee, AD/AC 1.1%, LAINF 0.7–1.5%) and Ticino cantonal rates. ### Cost of living and housing
Lazzate offers significantly lower purchase and rental prices than the most popular Ticino areas (Lugano, Ascona, Locarno). Prices vary depending on the area of the municipality, proximity to the border and local infrastructure. However, the housing differential must be strictly compared with the additional costs of daily commuting.
Approximate estimate of additional monthly costs: fuel CHF 150–300 (dependent on frequency and distance), car maintenance increase 25–30% (about CHF 50 per month), motorway tolls CHF 80–120, parking in Ticino CHF 100–200 in urban centres, car insurance CHF 100–150 per month (highest premiums in Italy). The Swiss vignette costs CHF 40 per year.
Not all economic scenarios are beneficial for relocation. It depends on personal factors: gross salary, number of actual working days in Ticino (partial teleworking changes the calculation), family composition (spouse, children, dependent parents), and specific housing costs in Lazzate compared to the target Ticino area. A monoredit family with children might find overall convenience; a young couple without children might find that housing savings are nullified by transportation costs and wasted time.
For a realistic and personalized estimate, use our [calcolatore costo della vita Ticino vs Italia](nav:cost-of-living).
### Advantages of moving to Lazzate
- Real estate prices
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### Taxation for cross-border workers: the New 2024 Agreement
The cross-border worker living in Lazzate and working in Ticino is subject to **withholding tax in Switzerland** (deducted by the employer directly from the paycheck). There is no double taxation because Italy avoids double taxation by applying a tax credit in the CE section of the 730 declaration (income model). The Italian-Swiss Convention, signed on December 9, 1976, regulates this aspect: the income from employment is taxed exclusively in the State where it is carried out (Switzerland).
The New Cross-Border Workers Agreement, which came into force on January 1, 2024 (ratified by Italy with Law 83 of June 13, 2023), has introduced different regimes for taxation and refunds:
- Old cross-border workers (already such before July 17, 2023): have the right to an exemption of €7,500 annually on employment income, a transitional regime that lasts until December 31, 2033 - New cross-border workers (starting after July 17, 2023): have an allowance of €10,000 annually
This distinction has significant impacts on refunds and annual liquidity. The lower the income, the more the allowance/exemption positively affects the tax result.
### Procedure and critical deadlines
1. Request Permit G Contact the SEM (State Secretariat for Migration) in the canton of Ticino (offices in Chiasso, Lugano, Bellinzona). Provide a letter of employment, employment contract, Italian identity document, certificate of residence in Lazzate. Processing time 2–4 weeks. Validity 1 year, renewable in January of each year.
2. INPS registration and change of address Communicate the new Italian address to the employer. Register with the INPS (National Institute for Social Security) cross-border management. Deadline: within 30 days of the change of residence.
3. Italian tax declaration (model 730) Complete the 730 model indicating the foreign employment income. Attach the Swiss tax certificate (Verrechnungssteuerbeleg) issued by the employer. Complete the CE section (foreign tax credit). Deadline: by May of the following year (or by November for 730-4).
4. Refund declaration If the Swiss employer has withheld more taxes than due, you can request a refund. Process with the Refund Declaration at the Italian Revenue Agency. Deadline: within the ordinary declaration terms.
The LAMal (Swiss health insurance) is mandatory. As a cross-border worker with Permit G, you have the right to choose: you can insure with a Swiss fund (adults' deductible CHF 300–2500 according to the plan) or maintain an Italian insurance, provided you notify the SEM.
Learn more about the procedures with our [Permit G cross-border workers guide](nav:permits) and use our [cross-border salary calculator](nav:calculator) to simulate your net monthly salary considering Swiss taxation, Italian refunds, and the allowance of the New 2024 Agreement.

item.title: Living in Cossogno and working in Ticino: border guide
item.description: From taxation to the cost of living: everything you need to know to live in Cossogno and work in Ticino as a border worker.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - New Cross-Border Agreement effective from 1 January 2024 - Withholding tax deducted ONLY in Switzerland for cross-border workers - Tax exemption: €7,500 (existing cross-border workers), €10,000 (new) - LAMal mandatory with option right for cross-border workers with G permit
## Key facts - **What**: Living in Cossogno (Italy) and working in Ticino as a cross-border worker - When: From 1 January 2024 (New Cross-Border Agreement in effect) - Where: Cossogno, province of Verbano-Cusio-Ossola, Ticino border - Who: Cross-border workers with G permit and registered with INPS - Tax regime: Exemption €7,500–€10,000 in Italy; withholding tax in Switzerland
Cossogno, a municipality in the province of Verbano-Cusio-Ossola on the shores of Lake Maggiore, attracts cross-border workers who work in the Canton of Ticino. This territory, located a few kilometers from the Ticino border, combines the quality of Italian life with access to the Swiss job market. From 1 January 2024, the New Cross-Border Agreement has redrawn the tax regime and benefits, making advance planning more important than ever.
### The tax regime after the New Agreement For cross-border workers already registered with the special INPS management before 17 July 2023, the Agreement provides an annual tax exemption of €7,500, included in a transitional regime that continues until 2033. New cross-border workers, on the other hand, benefit from a higher allowance: €10,000 per year. These amounts apply to employment income and represent the gross amount exempt from ordinary Italian taxation. The withholding tax on income is deducted exclusively by Switzerland, at the place of work. Italy avoids double taxation through the tax credit in the CE section of the [tax return (730)](nav:tax-return), a mechanism consolidated by the Italian-Swiss Convention of 9 December 1976. This means that the cross-border worker does not pay taxes on two fronts: Switzerland withholds at source, Italy applies the allowance and the credit for the Swiss withholding. Note: the exemption does not cover capital income, interest, or income other than employment income. A cross-border worker who has investments, securities, or rented properties will have to declare these incomes in Italy according to ordinary regulations.
### Contributions and social security in Switzerland As an employee in Ticino, the cross-border worker accumulates pension rights in the Swiss system. The contributions to AVS (Old Age and Survivors' Insurance) and AI (Disability Insurance) amount to 5.3% for the employee. To these are added the contribution for IPG (Loss of Earnings Allowance) and unemployment/crisis insurance (AD/AC), equal to 1.1% up to the limit of CHF 148,200 of annual salary. The LAINF (Accident Insurance) varies between 0.7% and 1.5%, depending on the professional risk category. If the annual salary exceeds CHF 21,330, the obligation to register with the Professional Pension (LPP, second pillar) is triggered, with contribution rates from 7% to 18% depending on the age group of the worker. The Italian INPS does not intervene for employment income in Switzerland, but the cross-border worker retains the rights accumulated in previous periods, creating a situation of double pension that must be coordinated at retirement.
### Health insurance and medical coverage
Those who live in Cossogno but work in Ticino must enroll in a [Swiss health insurance (LAMal)](nav:health). Cross-border workers with a G permit have the option to maintain Italian coverage from INPS or switch to a Swiss LAMal. Many opt for LAMal to align their protection with their workplace and to access Swiss healthcare services directly.
Deductibles for adults range from CHF 300 to CHF 2,500 annually, depending on the contract and chosen insurance fund. Monthly premiums vary significantly among insurers: comparing three to four offers is essential to control costs. From the perspective of a cross-border worker residing in Italy, LAMal provides immediate coverage for care in Ticino during working hours, while the Italian system remains available for services on rest days in Cossogno.
### Pension and supplementary pension savings
Cross-border workers accumulate pension rights in the Swiss system according to AVS/AI contributions. Occupational Pension (LPP) applies to all employees with an annual salary above CHF 21,330. The LPP contribution rate varies from 7% to 18% depending on the age bracket, with the burden shared between the employee and the employer.
Many cross-border workers supplement their pension strategy with the third pillar (3a), a Swiss tax deduction tool that allows annual contributions up to CHF 7,040 (2024 data) for employees. The Italian INPS accumulates rights in parallel as a secondary effect of contributions during the pre-cross-border period, creating a complex situation that requires coordination at retirement. Consulting an international pension expert is not a luxury but a practical necessity.
### Advantages of choosing Cossogno
- **Lower cost of living**: Housing, groceries, and local services cost less compared to Ticino - Tax protection: Swiss salary with cross-border exemption (€7,500–€10,000) in Italy - Established Italian community: Opportunity to maintain social and cultural networks in the home territory - Integrated healthcare access: LAMal for emergencies in Ticino, INPS for routine care in Italy - Attractive landscape: High-quality natural environment (Lake Maggiore, mountains)
### Concrete disadvantages and constraints
- Daily commuting: Early departure times, wait times at border crossings during peak periods, dependence on weather conditions, and potential alpine road closures - Administrative complexity: Parallel management of two tax, pension, and healthcare systems with different deadlines - Additional costs: Fuel, Swiss vignette, car insurance, potential tolls, increased mechanical wear - Social isolation: Reduced participation in the Ticinese community during non-working hours - Mobility constraints: Changing employers in Ticino or relocating the job requires reassessing the sustainability of commuting times
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### Practical checklist: what to verify before moving
The decision to live in Cossogno and start as a cross-border worker requires an ordered sequence of administrative steps. Each of them is not optional but necessary to avoid fiscal and legal surprises.
1. Registration with the special INPS management If not already registered, register with INPS for the special cross-border management. This registration determines your legal status and access to the tax exemption. The registration date is crucial: if before July 17, 2023, you receive €7,500 annually; if later, €10,000.
2. Request for the G permit The cross-border work permit (G) is managed by the canton of work (Ticino). Coordinate with your employer for the request to the cantonal authorities, or contact SECO at the federal level. For new permits after January 1, 2024, verify the requirements of the company agreement.
3. Choice of LAMal and communication Within 30 days of starting activity in Switzerland, register with a Swiss LAMal fund or communicate to INPS the intention to maintain Italian coverage. Collect quotes from at least three funds, comparing monthly premiums, deductibles, dental, and optical coverage.
4. Opening a Swiss bank account Many Ticino employers require a Swiss IBAN for salary payment. Choose a bank with an accessible branch (e.g., Locarno, Bellinzona), checking fees on CHF–EUR transfers and exchange rates. A second Italian account is useful for local expenses.
5. Tax estimate and declaration planning Use the [cross-border salary calculator](nav:calculator) to estimate the net post-Swiss tax and pre-Italian exemption. Plan the submission of the Italian 730 declaration (March–April of the following year), including the CE section for the tax credit on Swiss withholding.
6. Pension coordination Contact a pension advisor (at a union or Italian CAF) to understand the coordination between Swiss contributions and Italian payment periods. This advice is critical in case of future mobility.
7. Residential registration and documentation Keep the residential registration in Cossogno updated, communicate any address change to the Ticino employer, and keep documentation (residence certificates, employment letters, pay slips, Swiss tax receipts) for possible checks by the Italian Revenue Agency.
### Next steps: operational tools
The decision to move to Cossogno to work in Ticino is concretely feasible and thousands of cross-border workers do it every year. Early tax planning, correct administrative registration, and awareness of logistical constraints transform this choice into a tangible opportunity for quality of life and economic stability.
For a detailed estimate of your net based on the work profile, use the [cross-border salary calculator](nav:calculator). To clarify every regulatory aspect, consult the [complete guide to cross-border permits](nav:permits) before moving.

item.title: Living in Canzo and working in Ticino: border guide
item.description: Moving to Canzo to work in Ticino: New Agreement, G Permit, tax regime and practical checklist to start your border journey.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - New Cross-Border Workers Agreement in effect from January 1, 2024: exemption €7,500 (old cross-border workers), allowance €10,000 (new) - Withholding tax deducted only in Switzerland, no double taxation - Permit G required: application to SEM within 8 days of start date - AVS/LPP/LAMal guaranteed from the first day of work in Ticino
## Key facts - **What**: Cross-border workers tax regime with New Agreement - When: In effect from January 1, 2024 (Agreement signed December 23, 2020) - Where: Canton Ticino and border municipalities - Who: Italian G cross-border workers, managed by SEM/SECO - Exemption amount: €7,500 annually (old cross-border workers), €10,000 (new)
Canzo, in the province of Como, represents a concrete choice for those who want to work in Ticino while maintaining their Italian border residence. The New Cross-Border Workers Agreement, which came into effect on January 1, 2024, introduced a more advantageous tax regime for cross-border workers: old cross-border workers (those before July 17, 2023) benefit from an annual exemption of €7,500, while new cross-border workers have an allowance of €10,000. This change marks an important transition from the previous regime.
The Italian ratification of the Agreement took place with Law 83 of June 13, 2023. The withholding tax on employment income is deducted exclusively in Switzerland during the employment relationship — Italy completely avoids double taxation by applying a tax credit in the CE section of the 730 declaration. This means that the cross-border worker will pay taxes on their income only once.
### Subscribing to Permit G Anyone who decides to live in Canzo and work in Ticino must apply for Permit G with the State Secretariat for Migration (SEM). The application must be submitted within 8 days of the actual start date of the employment relationship in Switzerland. The SEM evaluates the request based on the availability of a confirmed job position by the Ticino employer and Italian registration documents. Once approved, Permit G authorizes the cross-border worker to reside in Italy and work in Switzerland for the duration of the contract (normally 12 months, renewable).
In terms of contributions, Old-Age and Survivors' Insurance (AVS), Disability Insurance (AI), Unemployment Insurance (AD), and Accident Insurance (LAINF) start from the first day of work. The Ticino employer makes the salary deductions according to the Swiss federal rates: AVS/AI/IPG at 5.3% for the employee, AD and AC at 1.1% (with maximum contributions based on CHF 148,200), LAINF from 0.7% to 1.5% depending on the sector.
### Deadlines and Dynamics of the Agreement The transitional regime of the Agreement runs from January 1, 2024, to December 31, 2033. During this decade, old cross-border workers maintain their favorable exemption, while new cross-border workers who sign after July 17, 2023, access the €10,000 allowance. After 2033, the transitional regime ends, and the definitive provisions, not yet fully specified in the current communication, will take effect. The Convention between Italy and Switzerland on double taxation, signed on December 9, 1976, remains the legal foundation that ensures the cross-border worker is not taxed twice on the same income. ### Distances, connections and commuting times from Canzo
Canzo is located in the province of Como, in a position halfway between the provincial capital and the Ticino border. Choosing to live in Canzo requires careful consideration of travel times to the workplace in Ticino — a critical factor for those who must repeat the journey daily. The main access routes from the Como area to the main Ticino crossings (Brogeda, Gaggiolo, Chiasso) involve journeys that vary depending on the final destination in Ticino (Mendrisio, Lugano, Bellinzona, Locarno).
The commuter living in the province of Como must consider the Italian road infrastructure and Swiss motorways (A2) to reach the workplace. Traffic jams at the crossings, especially during peak hours, can affect actual transit times. Each commuter must personally verify the route with their employer, calculating the actual travel time. A practical consideration is the choice of transportation: private car, public transport, or combined options. Using a car involves fuel costs, maintenance, parking in Ticino, and compliance with Swiss regulations.
### Cost of living and personal taxation
Canzo offers an overall lower cost of living compared to directly Swiss areas. The purchase of homes, local services (utilities, insurance, dining) follows Italian border prices, generally lower than those in Ticino. This difference is one of the main reasons why many commuters choose to live in Italy while maintaining Swiss income.
However, the commuter must consider additional expenses. Health insurance (LAMal), mandatory in Switzerland from the first day of work, has cantonal Ticino costs that vary with annual premiums. LAMal is not a health tax but a mandatory insurance with adult deductibles ranging from CHF 300 to CHF 2,500 depending on the chosen policy. The commuter with a G permit has the right to choose the Swiss insurer.
On an annual basis, the Italian IRPEF applies to the gross income earned in Switzerland according to progressive rates: 23% up to €28,000, 35% for the range €28,001–€50,000, 43% over €50,000. The Italian tax return (730) is completed by indicating in the CE section the Swiss tax credit, thus compensating for the withholdings from the Ticino salary.
### Advantages and disadvantages of choosing Canzo
The main advantages include: lower Italian cost of living compared to Ticino (especially for real estate and basic services); Swiss salary that maintains purchasing power in CHF (stable compared to EUR); full access to the AVS/LPP system (second Swiss pillar) and LAMal from the first day of work; favorable tax exemption regime on income according to the New Agreement (€7,500 for old commuters, €10,000 for new ones); geographical proximity to the border for daily movements.
The disadvantages include: non-negligible daily travel times due to distance and possible traffic jams at the crossings; vulnerability to temporary border closures (strikes, accidents, weather emergencies); direct commuting costs (fuel, car maintenance, parking); double regulation (Italian for residence, Swiss for work taxation and social contributions); need to manage two tax declarations (730 in Italy, registration with Ticino cantonal authorities).
## Useful tools for your case To verify your within/over 20 km tax scenario, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [tax return guide](nav:tax-return). ### Checklist: how to move and start working as a cross-border commuter
1. Verify the job offer and start date: The Ticino employer must provide an official letter of employment with the start date. The SEM requires this documentation for the Permesso G application.
2. Register with the SEM within 8 days of starting: The Permesso G application must reach the SEM (State Migration Office) within one week of the actual start date of work. Delays may result in administrative consequences.
3. **Collect Italian documentation**: Identity document, municipal residence certificate, certificate of pending charges. Local administrations in Canzo provide these documents.
4. Choose Swiss health insurance (LAMal): The cross-border commuter must enroll with a Swiss health insurance company based in Ticino. The choice of policy (and deductible: CHF 300–2,500) depends on the personal risk profile and available budget.

item.title: Mandello del Lario: 2024 Ticino border guide
item.description: Mandello del Lario in Lecco: how to live and work as a border worker in Ticino. Permit G, tax at source, deductible 2024, AVS/LAMal.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief
- Permit G: Italian residence, work in Ticino (within 30 km of the border). - New Cross-Border Workers Agreement: effective from January 1, 2024 for new cross-border workers. - 2024 Exemption: €10,000 (new) and €7,500 (old cross-border workers until 2033). - Taxed in Switzerland, double taxation avoided with Italian tax credit.
## Key facts
- **What**: Cross-border worker residing in Italy and employed in Ticino - When: From January 1, 2024 (New Cross-Border Workers Agreement) - Where: Mandello del Lario (Lecco) and Canton Ticino - Who: Cross-border workers admitted with permit G - Exemption: €10,000 annually (new), €7,500 (old until 2033)
---
The New Cross-Border Workers Agreement, signed on December 23, 2020 and ratified by Italy through Law 83 of June 13, 2023, came into force on January 1, 2024. For those residing in Mandello del Lario and working in Ticino, this agreement substantially transforms the tax and contributory regime.
### Tax advantages: exemption and exemptions
Starting from 2024, new cross-border workers (those who applied for permit G from July 17, 2023 onwards) benefit from an annual exemption of €10,000 on taxable income. This means that the first €10,000 of earnings in Ticino are not subject to Swiss withholding tax.
Old cross-border workers (already holders of permit G before July 17, 2023) retain a more advantageous exemption of €7,500 annually and keep this benefit until December 31, 2033, for a transitional regime that protects those already engaged in cross-border work.
For example, a new cross-border worker with an annual gross income of €45,000 in Ticino will have the withholding tax calculated on €35,000 (45 minus 10 of exemption), not on €45,000. This significantly reduces the Swiss tax burden from the first year.
### Withholding tax and double taxation mechanism
A crucial aspect for the cross-border worker from Mandello is understanding how taxation works. The withholding tax on employment income is withheld ONLY in Switzerland from the paycheck. Italy DOES NOT withhold taxes on income earned in Switzerland, pursuant to the Convention against Double Taxation Italy-Switzerland signed on December 9, 1976.
The Convention establishes that the right to tax employment income belongs to the State where the work is performed, i.e., Switzerland. Italy, consequently, grants a tax credit in the 730 form (CE section) to avoid the cross-border worker paying taxes twice on the same income. Therefore, a cross-border worker does not pay health insurance (LAMal) twice, nor taxes both in Switzerland and Italy.
### Permit G: the key to working from Mandello
Mandello del Lario is located in the province of Lecco, on Lake Como, a few kilometers from the main Italo-Swiss border crossings: Brogeda (Varese-Como-Ticino), Chiasso, and Gaggiolo. This geographical proximity makes Mandello a natural base for those wishing to work in Lugano, Mendrisio, Bellinzona, or other Ticino locations while maintaining Italian residence.
Permit G is the Swiss federal authorization (administered by the State Secretariat for Migration, SEM) that allows Italian citizens residing in a border area to work in Switzerland. It is territorially limited: work is permitted within a radius of about 30 km from the border line, a perimeter that covers the entire Canton Ticino. The procedure for obtaining permit G involves submitting the application to the Population Office of the Italian province (for Mandello, the Province of Lecco or the Prefecture) in coordination with the Swiss SEM. ## What changes concretely for the cross-border worker from 2024
The New Cross-Border Agreement is a step forward for those who live in Mandello and work in Ticino. Before 2024, a cross-border worker with an annual income of €45,000 in Ticino was subject to withholding tax on the entire amount. From 2024, the exemption of €10,000 (for new cross-border workers) reduces the taxable amount to €35,000, immediately decreasing the Swiss tax burden. You can check your net monthly income with the [salary calculator](nav:calculator).
### Pension contributions: AVS, LPP and pillars
The cross-border worker from Mandello pays pension contributions in Switzerland according to the Swiss three-pillar system. **AVS (old-age and survivors' insurance)**: the employer pays 5.3% of the gross salary as an employee contribution. The cross-border worker accumulates credits towards the Swiss pension, regardless of nationality.
LPP (occupational pension): from the age of 25, the employer pays for the LPP (second pillar) a contribution ranging from 7% to 18% depending on age. It is a form of pension savings, different from the Italian INPS.
Double payment: the cross-border worker also pays INPS contributions in Italy at 9.19% on the amount that does not exceed the exemption limits. The New Agreement limits this double contribution for new cross-border workers. Learn more about the [pension system](nav:pension).
### LAMal: health insurance
The cross-border worker must subscribe to a [health insurance (LAMal)](nav:health) with a Swiss insurer. Deductibles range from CHF 300 to CHF 2,500 per calendar year. A cross-border worker with a low deductible pays higher premiums, while one with a high deductible pays less. LAMal covers healthcare services in Ticino and, through bilateral agreements, also in Italy for emergencies.
### Practical procedure: how to move from Mandello
An Italian citizen residing in Mandello who intends to work in Ticino must: 1. Obtain a job offer from a Ticino employer. 2. Apply for a G permit at the Population Office of the Province of Lecco in coordination with the company. 3. The Swiss SEM authorizes the permit. 4. Subscribe to a Swiss health insurance (LAMal). 5. Present themselves on the first day of work with identity documents, Italian tax code, and Swiss insurance number.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ## Next steps: from Mandello to work in Ticino
If you are considering moving from Mandello del Lario to work in Ticino, these are the concrete steps that guide the process.
### Pre-move checklist
**Months 1-2: Research and offer** — Consult job search portals that publish positions in Ticino. Identify the company and obtain a written job offer. Verify the proposed gross salary and the sector (some sectors have different contributions).
Month 3: G permit application — Contact the Population Office of the Province of Lecco (your place of residence in Mandello). Fill out the G permit application form together with the Ticino company. Provide a copy of the job offer and your personal data (passport, Italian tax code). Submit the application coordinating with the company and the SEM.
Month 4: SEM authorization — The SEM examines the application and decides (usually in 4-6 weeks). If approved, the SEM issues the G permit and communicates it to the company and to you. The permit is valid for one year and is renewable.
Month 5: Health insurance — Register with a Swiss insurer for LAMal before starting work. Choose the deductible and coverage plan. Receive the insurance card.
Month 6: First day of work — Present identity documents, Italian tax code, G permit, and health insurance number. The employer will initiate procedures for registration with AVS/LPP/Swiss accident insurance. You will receive the first pay slip with withholding tax, AVS, LPP, and INPS contributions.
### Essential documents
For each step of the procedure, keep handy: valid Italian passport or identity document, Italian tax code, job offer signed by the Ticino company, proof of residence in Mandello (utility bill, rental/ownership contract), certificate of registration with Italian INPS (optional but recommended).
### Tools to monitor your situation
After the move, use these tools to check your tax and pension situation: Salary calculator simulates the net monthly amount based on the proposed gross and deductible. Tax return: at the end of the year, fill out the 730 form in Italy, including Swiss income in the CE section and tax credit. Contact INPS/Revenue Agency: for checks and clarifications on double taxation.
### Make an informed decision
Living in Mandello del Lario and working in Ticino is a conscious choice that requires understanding of tax and pension rules. The New Frontier Workers Agreement has improved the situation, but it is essential to verify your specific income scenario. Simulate your net salary using the [frontier worker calculator](nav:calculator) to check if the €10,000 deductible and the Swiss regime are actually advantageous for you. This simple step allows you to make an informed decision before moving.

item.title: Lambrugo: living and working in Ticino
item.description: Frontier from Lambrugo: practical guide on crossings, taxation, AVS and LAMal. Getting started, costs and benefits of Como-Ticino commuting.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - Living in Lambrugo allows Swiss wages with lower cost of living - Withholding tax withheld only in Switzerland, refills via form 730 - Compulsory AVS/LPP registration from the first day; LAMal with the right to choose - Access via the Brogeda, Chiasso, Gaggiolo, Ponte Tresa passes
## Key facts - **Chi**: cross-border commuters resident in the province of Como, G permit - What: work in Canton Ticino as an Italian resident - When: starting from the New Frontier Agreement (1 January 2024) - Where: passes Brogeda–Gaggiolo, Chiasso, Ponte Tresa - Tax at source: withheld in Switzerland, no double taxation - New frontier worker deductible: CHF 10,000 per year - Excess for old frontier workers: CHF 7,500 (transitory until 2033)
Lambrugo, a municipality in the province of Como, is located a few kilometres from the Ticino border. For those who choose to live here while working in Ticino, the geographical location offers a concrete economic opportunity: Swiss wages, structurally reduced taxes, Italian cost of living. But the status of border worker entails specific tax and social security obligations that must be understood before moving.
The G permit is the standard authorisation for frontier workers from the province of Como. From January 2024, with the entry into force of the New Frontier Agreement (signed on 23 December 2020), new frontier workers benefit from an income allowance of CHF 10,000 per annum in Switzerland. ### Connection to Border Crossings and Travel Times
Lambrugo is located in the Province of Como, west of Lake Como. Access to the main border crossings towards Ticino is provided through:
- **Brogeda** (Stabio–Gaggiolo): the southernmost crossing, connecting the Province of Como to the Mendrisiotto - Chiasso: the main road border between Como and Ticino, with heavy commuter traffic flows - Ponte Tresa: a crossing on Lake Lugano (Ceresio), more convenient for those working in the Varese–Lugano area - Gaggiolo: crossing towards the Locarnese
Travel times from Lambrugo to the main Ticino employment hubs (Lugano, Mendrisio, Bellinzona, Locarno) vary depending on the border crossing and final destination. During peak hours (early morning, late afternoon), traffic at the border crossings can cause significant delays. It is advisable to [check border crossing times and conditions](nav:border) in real time before planning departure times.
### Transportation and Logistics Costs
Those who choose a private car for commuting must consider several recurring expenses. Fuel and car maintenance represent the most variable costs; third-party liability insurance must cover driving both in Switzerland and in Italy. The Swiss motorway vignette costs CHF 40 per calendar year and allows circulation on all Swiss motorways.
In some sections (A2 Gotthard, A9 Mendrisiotto), additional tolls may be applied. Most employers in Ticino offer free parking or a flat-rate fee at the workplace.
Alternatively, you can check [public transport](nav:transport) options via Trenord trains (Como–Chiasso), local buses, and SBB railways in Ticino. This solution can be competitive if the final destinations are well served by train stations or bus stops.
### Cost of Living: Lambrugo vs Canton Ticino
Living in Lambrugo (Province of Como) offers a lower cost of living compared to Ticino across several categories. Residential rent is generally 20–40% lower than in comparable Ticino cities such as Lugano, Mendrisio, or Bellinzona. Differences in food prices are modest; utility costs (gas, electricity) vary according to Italian legislation. Property taxes (IUC) are frequently lower than Ticino cantonal taxes.
This cost-of-living differential partly offsets recurring commuting expenses (fuel, vignette, car wear), making residence in the Province of Como economically convenient for those earning in Swiss francs.
## Useful tools for your case To verify your within/over 20 km tax scenario, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [tax return guide](nav:tax-return). ### Tax declaration and refunds: from Form 730 to the tax credit
Once resident in Italy and working as a cross-border worker in Ticino, the annual income tax declaration is submitted through Form 730 (or Form Unico if you carry out self-employed activities). In section CE you must report foreign employment income (i.e. Swiss income) and the tax credit corresponding to the withholding tax paid in Switzerland. This mechanism avoids double taxation.
The amount of Swiss withholding tax is used as a credit against the Italian tax owed. Frequently the cross-border worker receives a refund, i.e. the reimbursement of the difference between the Swiss tax paid and the Italian tax owed, because Swiss rates are generally lower than Italian progressive rates (IRPEF).
The declaration must be submitted: - Through the Agenzia delle Entrate website, the desktop app, or via a CAF (Tax Assistance Centre) - Within the ordinary deadlines set each year (usually May for Form 730) - Together with documentation of the Swiss payslip (annual tax certificate, gross income certificate)
### Step-by-step: how to start as a cross-border worker from Lambrugo
The operational steps are sequential and require coordination between the Swiss employer, cantonal authorities and municipalities:
1. Look for a job in Ticino and sign an employment contract with the Swiss employer 2. Apply for a G permit from the Ticino cantonal authorities (competent department) or at the district office. The Swiss employer will assist you with the procedure and the documentation 3. Register with AVS/LPP through the employer, by the first day of work. Registration is mandatory 4. Choose LAMal insurance with an authorised Swiss insurer. Cross-border workers with a G permit have the right to choose between insurers 5. Notify the change of residence to the Italian municipality of registration (if you are moving from another town to Lambrugo) and obtain a residence certificate 6. Open a bank account with a bank that accepts cross-border customers. Check the affiliated banks that offer specific services for cross-border workers, as not all of them provide this service 7. Plan your annual tax declaration with an Italian accountant or CAF specialised in cross-border income
### Change of registered residence and housing matters
Transferring your registered residence from an Italian municipality to Lambrugo is a municipal administrative procedure. You must: - Submit a change-of-residence declaration at the registry office (ufficio anagrafe) of the municipality of Lambrugo - Have a verifiable housing address (rental with a registered contract, property ownership, free loan) - Receive the residence certificate
This certificate is essential for the G permit registration and for the correct tax declaration in Italy. Finally, it is strongly advisable to contact a tax consultant specialised in cross-border workers or an accounting firm to optimise the management of Swiss income, Italian tax deductions and social security contributions.
